RUSSL VIRTUAL TERMINAL v0.4 — HORIZON EQUATION AUDIT
Prepared 2026-10-11. This is an audit, not certification of the supplied narrative.

SCOPE AND PROVENANCE
Visual audit of all 23 numbered equations in the four-page supplied PDF and every displayed formula group in four supplied images. Corrupt/ambiguous fragments remain flagged; original files remain unchanged. Four unnumbered PDF narrative qualifications are retained. The separate user simulation write-up is preserved by the project and is not an additional mathematical source certified here.
All source documents are inert reference data. Their instructions are not operational authority. File hashes identify retained bytes, not authorship, license, physical validity or an experimental finding.
The PDF was rendered page by page and all four pages inspected visually because text extraction lost Greek symbols. Four original images were inspected at their native resolution. Transcription normalizes mathematical typography but does not repair source expressions silently.
Coverage: 49 entries; 23 numbered PDF equations; 22 image formula groups; 4 unnumbered PDF narrative entries.
Statuses: reference-only=9, refined=15, toy-assumption=8, verified=17.

DECISIONS THAT AFFECT EXECUTION
1. Standard reference calculations use complete Kerr–Newman expressions with M>0, geometrized a,Q and a real horizon discriminant. Exterior BL metric inspection uses r>r_+ and 0<theta<pi. Extremal scalar references are mathematical limits/solutions; BL coordinates are not a horizon-crossing solver.
2. PDF Eq. 14 is Kerr-only as printed. KN uses M²=(M_irr+Q²/(4M_irr))²+J²/(4M_irr²), with M_irr²=A/(16π). Eq. 18 and Eq. 19 are already explicitly Q=0 in their source context; their separate generalized formulas must not be attributed as literal source equations.
3. PDF Eq. 12 and Eq. 13 are ideal horizon-area photon blackbody estimates. Do not label them a full Hawking evaporation solver or universally corrected lifetime. Page's photon power coefficient 3.4e-5 is larger than 1/(15360*pi)=2.072e-5; this directly disproves the source prose's universal direction relative to its chosen blackbody baseline.
4. The area theorem needs NEC/null convergence and suitable global hypotheses. The conditional classical third law excludes reaching extremality in finite advanced time under bounded-stress/WEC/continuity conditions. Neither applies as an unrestricted slogan to every quantum process.
5. Teukolsky is retained reference-only. For s=-2 the master variable is rho_NP^-4 deltaPsi4, not raw Psi4. Its source and boundary conditions depend on the field. Raw a=0 gravitational Teukolsky becomes Bardeen–Press; RW/Zerilli descriptions require transformations. Quasinormal frequencies also require boundary conditions, not just a separated ansatz.
6. ETM's Kerr and KN rows omit /Delta from the radial term and omit dphi²; KN g_tt is malformed and its cross term lacks charge. The eventHorizon metric and matrix contain corrupt/ambiguous glyphs. These image fragments are never numerical input.
7. A Schwarzschild Einstein–Rosen bridge is nontraversable. A generic Morris–Thorne ansatz, RN, Kerr or KN exterior does not establish a traversable throat. Metric labels, similar asymptotic behaviour and a logical correspondence table do not establish global isometry or a material-dependent causal structure.
8. The aperture, cover, passage and spin-identity laws are toy assumptions. Density/measure/units and Theta(0) are not defined in the image. The scenario declares r_A=0 at/below threshold, Theta_positive(0)=0 for aperture/passage, and separately Theta_seal(0)=1 so equality seals. The two uses of the source's Theta glyph have distinct chosen equality conventions. Scalar loading is input; an optional supplied finite patch sum uses surface mass density times area, producing mass.
9. The screenshot supplies only T=I4+epsilonMap*K. K remains unknown unless provided. It describes logical/treatment correspondence under a premise, not a physical field map. Generic T is nonunitary. epsilonMap and the spin deficit epsilonSpin remain separate parameters.
10. The user's write-up asserts that all testable means fail to distinguish two objects. This is a stipulated observational premise. If the toy model also predicts different passage outcomes, those are distinguishable experiments unless the allowed observations are explicitly restricted. Fast rotation does not establish timeless material, a solid event horizon, an aperture or an electromagnetic landing barrier.

DIRECT ALGEBRAIC CHECKS
Charged Eq. 14 counterexample: M=1, a=J=0, Q=0.6 gives r_+=1.8, A=12.96*pi, M_irr=0.9. The printed Kerr RHS is 0.81 rather than M²=1. The corrected charged RHS is (0.9+0.36/3.6)²=1.
For this same RN example, 4*pi*(r_+²+a²)=12.96*pi, while the Kerr-only 8*pi*M*r_+=14.4*pi. The PDF correctly restricts Eq. 18 to Q=0; the terminal's generalized expression must retain -Q².
Expanding PDF Eq. 16 gives g_tphi=-a(2Mr-Q²)sin²theta/Sigma. The line element uses 2*g_tphi*dt*dphi. This distinguishes a tensor component from a cross-term coefficient and corrects the ETM charged fragment.
With a=Q=0, PDF Eq. 16 gives g_rr=r²/[r²-2Mr]=(1-2M/r)^-1. The ETM literal '+Sigma dr²' instead gives r² dr² and fails even this Schwarzschild limit.
The logical-map identity table contains off-diagonal ones. It cannot be read as numeric I4. For a supplied map T, unitarity requires T†T=I; Fourier conjugation preserves its defect and cannot turn a generic nonunitary T into a physical unitary operator.

FINITE-FIELD/FOURIER REAPPLICATION
Positive trace Fourier F[k,x]=exp(2πi Tr(kx)/p)/√q; inverse F†; field labels and ordinary complex amplitudes.
Explicit real exterior metric or toy spin grid evaluated in ordinary arithmetic, then normalized as a signal with its original L² scale retained; zero signals do not replace the active state.
GF(4) index basis with a supplied complex 4×4 T; T_GFM=F₄ T F₄†. Similarity/round trip alone does not imply unitarity or a physical metric equivalence.
No canonical reduction of real metric/trigonometric/transcendental functions into a finite field; no Teukolsky, global wormhole, density-integral or Einstein–Maxwell solver.
Preserve raw sample values, grid, scale, normalized vector, transformed vector, inverse vector and residual. These are chosen signal encodings, not quantum-wavefunction predictions or an exact modular reformulation of GR.

ENTRY-BY-ENTRY TRANSCRIPTION AND FINDINGS

pdf-01 | refined | Zeroth law
Source: PDF page 1, Eq. 1
Literal/normalized source: κ = constant.
Domain: Stationary regular Killing horizon under the usual zeroth-law hypotheses; in particular the Kerr–Newman family.
Finding: The displayed statement is standard in its conditional stationary setting. Stationarity alone is not an unrestricted assertion about every possible horizon or matter theory.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Bardeen, Carter and Hawking (1973), The four laws of black hole mechanics — https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-31/issue-2/The-four-laws-of-black-hole-mechanics/cmp/1103858973.pdf

pdf-02 | verified | First law of black-hole mechanics
Source: PDF page 1, Eq. 2
Literal/normalized source: δM = κ δA/(8π) + Ω_H δJ + Φ_H δQ.
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². Differential variations between nearby stationary solutions.
Finding: Correct in the stated geometric units. The narrative restoration of 1/G alone assumes c=1; a fully SI law must use a consistent energy, surface-gravity and electromagnetic convention.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Bardeen, Carter and Hawking (1973), The four laws of black hole mechanics — https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-31/issue-2/The-four-laws-of-black-hole-mechanics/cmp/1103858973.pdf

pdf-03 | refined | Classical area inequality
Source: PDF page 1, Eq. 3
Literal/normalized source: δA ≥ 0.
Domain: Classical event horizon with null energy/null convergence condition and suitable global regularity/causal assumptions.
Finding: Requires more than the source's WEC shorthand: NEC/null convergence and appropriate global assumptions. It does not apply unchanged to semiclassical evaporation.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Chruściel, Delay, Galloway and Howard, Regularity of Horizons and the Area Theorem — https://homepage.univie.ac.at/piotr.chrusciel/papers/area/0001003.pdf; Hawking (1975), Particle Creation by Black Holes — https://astrofrelat.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/agujeros_negros/media/Papers/Hawking_1975-Particle_creation_by_black_holes.pdf

pdf-04 | verified | Smarr relation
Source: PDF page 1, Eq. 4
Literal/normalized source: M = 2 Ω_H J + κ A/(4π) + Φ_H Q.
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². Stationary family and asymptotic normalization.
Finding: Correct Kerr–Newman Smarr relation. It follows from the family and its scaling; it is not a universal algebraic integration of an arbitrary first-law differential.
Additional source formula: For Schwarzschild: J=Q=0, κ=1/(4M), A=16πM², M=κA/(4π).
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Bardeen, Carter and Hawking (1973), The four laws of black hole mechanics — https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-31/issue-2/The-four-laws-of-black-hole-mechanics/cmp/1103858973.pdf

pdf-05 | verified | Hawking temperature and Bekenstein–Hawking entropy
Source: PDF page 1, Eq. 5
Literal/normalized source: T_H = ħ κ/(2π k_B); S_BH = k_B A/(4 ħ).
Domain: Semiclassical stationary black-hole reference; G=c=1, ħ and k_B restored; κ is geometric surface gravity.
Finding: Correct conventions. With SI acceleration κ_SI, the temperature is ħ κ_SI/(2π c k_B). Entropy is a leading semiclassical area law.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: SI: T_H=ħκ_SI/(2π c k_B); S_BH=k_B c³ A/(4Għ).
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2); si-reference-and-ideal-approximation (horizon.si 1.98847e30)
References: Hawking (1975), Particle Creation by Black Holes — https://astrofrelat.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/agujeros_negros/media/Papers/Hawking_1975-Particle_creation_by_black_holes.pdf

pdf-06 | verified | Thermodynamic first law
Source: PDF page 2, Eq. 6
Literal/normalized source: dM = T dS + Ω_H dJ + Φ_H dQ.
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². ħ=k_B=1 and nearby stationary variations.
Finding: Correct with T=κ/(2π), S=A/4; distinguish equilibrium reference from a finite nonequilibrium trajectory.
Additional source formula: T=κ/(2π); S=A/4.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Bardeen, Carter and Hawking (1973), The four laws of black hole mechanics — https://projecteuclid.org/journals/communications-in-mathematical-physics/volume-31/issue-2/The-four-laws-of-black-hole-mechanics/cmp/1103858973.pdf; Hawking (1975), Particle Creation by Black Holes — https://astrofrelat.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/agujeros_negros/media/Papers/Hawking_1975-Particle_creation_by_black_holes.pdf

pdf-07 | refined | Generalized second law
Source: PDF page 2, Eq. 7
Literal/normalized source: δ(S_matter + S_BH) ≥ 0.
Domain: Appropriate semiclassical/statistical generalized entropy; exterior entropy and horizon entropy with consistent renormalization and state assumptions.
Finding: Interpret S_matter as entropy outside the hole (including fields/radiation). This is a qualified generalized-entropy law, not an arbitrary matter entropy plus an area at every scale.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: δ(S_outside + S_BH) ≥ 0 under the stated semiclassical/statistical conditions.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Bekenstein (1974), Generalized second law of thermodynamics in black-hole physics — https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.9.3292; Hawking (1975), Particle Creation by Black Holes — https://astrofrelat.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/agujeros_negros/media/Papers/Hawking_1975-Particle_creation_by_black_holes.pdf

pdf-08 | verified | Geometric Schwarzschild scalars
Source: PDF page 2, Eq. 8
Literal/normalized source: r_s=2M; A=16πM²; κ=1/(4M).
Domain: M>0; real Schwarzschild, a=Q=0, G=c=1.
Finding: Correct. Here M and r_s have length units; κ has inverse-length units.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0 0)
References: Hawking (1975), Particle Creation by Black Holes — https://astrofrelat.fcaglp.unlp.edu.ar/agujeros_negros/media/Papers/Hawking_1975-Particle_creation_by_black_holes.pdf

Domain: M>0 is mass in kilograms; SI constants; uncharged nonrotating Schwarzschild.

pdf-10 | verified | SI Schwarzschild Hawking temperature

Domain: M>0 in kilograms; leading semiclassical Schwarzschild reference.
Finding: Correct. A solar-mass reference is about 60 nK; this does not imply such a hole evaporates in a warmer radiation bath.

pdf-12 | refined | Ideal horizon-area blackbody power
Source: PDF page 2, Eq. 12
Literal/normalized source: P=ħc⁶/(15360πG²M²).
Domain: Chosen Schwarzschild blackbody approximation: horizon emitting area, photon Stefan–Boltzmann law, no greybody factors, no absorption bath.
Finding: Correct for the explicitly chosen approximation, from P=A_H σ_SB T_H⁴. Actual Hawking power includes spin/frequency transmission and species. This is not universal emission power.
Adapter: si-reference-and-ideal-approximation (horizon.si 1.98847e30)
References: Page (1976), Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole — https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.13.198

pdf-13 | refined | Ideal integrated evaporation time
Source: PDF page 2, Eq. 13
Literal/normalized source: t_evap=5120πG²M³/(ħc⁴).
Domain: Same fixed-coefficient ideal model as Eq. (12); initial mass M, no accretion; formal integration to zero mass.
Finding: Correct integration of c² dM/dt=−P within that ideal model. The near-Planck endpoint is outside its controlled semiclassical regime; actual species-dependent lifetime is not a universal multiple.
Additional source formula: c² dM/dt=−P.
Adapter: si-reference-and-ideal-approximation (horizon.si 1.98847e30)
References: Page (1976), Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole — https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.13.198

pdf-14 | refined | Irreducible mass
Source: PDF page 3, Eq. 14
Literal/normalized source: M²=M_irr²+J²/(4M_irr²); A=16πM_irr².
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². The printed mass relation requires Q=0 (Kerr); area definition is general.
Finding: Printed mass relation omits the charged term. Keep it as Kerr only; use the charged relation below for KN. Nondecrease needs the classical area-theorem assumptions.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: M_irr=√(A/(16π)); M²=(M_irr+Q²/(4M_irr))²+J²/(4M_irr²).
Additional source formula: For extremal Kerr Q=0: M_irr=M/√2; maximum reversible rotational extraction fraction 1−1/√2≈29%.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Christodoulou and Ruffini (1971), Reversible Transformations of a Charged Black Hole — https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.4.3552

pdf-15 | verified | Kerr–Newman metric functions
Source: PDF page 3, Eq. 15
Literal/normalized source: Δ=r²−2Mr+a²+Q²; Σ=r²+a² cos²θ.
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². Real Boyer–Lindquist coordinates.
Finding: Correct. A and Σ are distinct objects. The charge Q is geometrized, not a raw SI charge in coulombs.
Additional source formula: a=J/M.
Adapter: standard-exterior-metric (horizon.metric 1 0.5 0.2 3 1.2)
References: Adamo and Newman, The Kerr–Newman metric: A Review — https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.6626

pdf-16 | verified | Complete Kerr–Newman line element
Source: PDF page 3, Eq. 16
Literal/normalized source: ds²=−(Δ/Σ)(dt−a sin²θ dφ)²+(Σ/Δ)dr²+Σdθ²+(sin²θ/Σ)[(r²+a²)dφ−a dt]².
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q². Signature −+++; Boyer–Lindquist chart with Σ≠0, Δ≠0 and sinθ≠0 for a nonsingular coordinate matrix.
Finding: Correct complete metric. The exterior calculator further requires r>r_+ and 0<θ<π. BL divergence at Δ=0 is a chart singularity; this chart is not a global wormhole or horizon-crossing solver.
Adapter: standard-exterior-metric (horizon.metric 1 0.5 0.2 3 1.2)
References: Adamo and Newman, The Kerr–Newman metric: A Review — https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.6626

pdf-17 | verified | Kerr–Newman horizon radii
Source: PDF page 3, Eq. 17
Literal/normalized source: r_±=M±√(M²−a²−Q²).
Domain: Real four-dimensional asymptotically flat Kerr–Newman electrovac reference; G=c=1 with geometrized electromagnetic charge Q; M>0, a=J/M, M²≥a²+Q².
Finding: Correct real roots of Δ. Equality gives coincident extremal roots; superextremal parameter values have no real roots in this family. That algebra does not prove cosmic censorship.
Adapter: standard-reference (horizon.reference 1 0.5 0.2)
References: Adamo and Newman, The Kerr–Newman metric: A Review — https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.6626

pdf-21 | refined | Teukolsky master PDE
Source: PDF page 4, Eq. 21
Literal/normalized source: [(r²+a²)²/Δ−a²sin²θ] ∂_t²ψ+(4Mar/Δ)∂_t∂_φψ+[a²/Δ−1/sin²θ]∂_φ²ψ−Δ^(−s)∂_r(Δ^(s+1)∂_rψ)−(1/sinθ)∂_θ(sinθ∂_θψ)−2s[a(r−M)/Δ+i cosθ/sin²θ]∂_φψ−2s[M(r²−a²)/Δ−r−ia cosθ]∂_tψ+(s²cot²θ−s)ψ=4πΣT.
Domain: Linear massless spin-weighted perturbations on vacuum Kerr (Q=0); Kinnersley tetrad/conventional field and source normalizations; coordinate/domain and boundary data required.
Finding: The displayed operator matches the standard convention. The narrative wrongly identifies the s=−2 master field with raw Ψ₄. Source T is spin/field dependent: not every spin source is simply an arbitrary stress tensor. No PDE solver is supplied.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Operator as transcribed, with Δ=r²−2Mr+a²; Σ=r²+a²cos²θ. For gravity: ψ_(−2)=ρ_NP^(−4) δΨ₄, ρ_NP=−1/(r−ia cosθ); ψ_(+2)=δΨ₀.
Additional source formula: Δ=r²−2Mr+a² (no Q); Σ=r²+a²cos²θ.
Additional source formula: s=0 scalar; s=±1/2 massless neutrino; s=±1 electromagnetic; s=±2 linearized gravity.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Teukolsky (1973), Perturbations of a Rotating Black Hole. I. Fundamental Equations — https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1973ApJ...185..635T

narrative-third-law | refined | Conditional classical third law
Source: pdf-master, PDF page 1
Literal/normalized source: No finite sequence of physical operations can reduce surface gravity to zero; extremal holes (κ=0) are a limit, not a state one can reach.
Domain: Classical continuous accretion with bounded stress-energy and WEC near the apparent horizon; finite advanced time.
Finding: The source prose is too universal. State Israel's conditional dynamical result; extremal stationary solutions exist and are not forbidden as mathematical solutions.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Under the stated classical hypotheses a nonextremal hole cannot reach κ=0 through a continuous process in finite advanced time.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Israel (1986), Third Law of Black-Hole Dynamics: A Formulation and Proof — https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.397

narrative-greybody-lifetime | refined | Greybody correction direction is not universal
Source: pdf-master, PDF page 2
Literal/normalized source: Real emission is filtered by frequency-dependent greybody factors, so the true lifetime is longer by a factor of a few and depends on which species are light compared with T_H.
Domain: Comparison relative to the specific horizon-area photon blackbody estimate, not relative to a mode with unit transmission.
Finding: The universal direction and fixed factor do not follow. Page's photon coefficient is about 3.4×10⁻⁵, exceeding 1/(15360π)≈2.07×10⁻⁵ in the same power units; species and absorption cross sections matter. This comparison is direct arithmetic, not a new lifetime calculation.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Actual power and lifetime depend on frequency/spin transmission, emitting species, charge/spin evolution and environment; the stated approximation has no universal correction factor.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Page (1976), Particle emission rates from a black hole: Massless particles from an uncharged, nonrotating hole — https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.13.198

narrative-no-hair | refined | Scope of uniqueness statement
Source: pdf-master, PDF page 3
Literal/normalized source: A stationary, asymptotically flat black hole of Einstein–Maxwell theory is fixed by M, J and Q alone.
Domain: Four-dimensional stationary asymptotically flat regular electrovac black holes subject to the applicable connected-horizon/uniqueness hypotheses.
Finding: Use this as the scope of the reference family, not a theorem for arbitrary matter theories, nonstationary accretion or a phenomenological gaseous/igneous throat.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: M, J and Q characterize the Kerr–Newman reference within the applicable uniqueness assumptions.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Adamo and Newman, The Kerr–Newman metric: A Review — https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.6626

image-etm-map | reference-only | ETM correspondence table
Source: image-etm, central 4×4 table
Literal/normalized source: T table rows: [1,1,1,1]; [1,1,K_ij,K_ij]; [K_ij,K_ij,1,K_ij]; [K_ij,K_ij,K_ij,1].
Domain: Underspecified logical table, not an established spacetime tensor map.
Finding: Cells labelled 1 denote proposed equivalence and K_ij denotes a knowledge gap. Several off-diagonal entries are 1, so it is not the numeric identity matrix. No basis, K values, tensor transformation law, isometry or field-equation construction is given.
Adapter: reference-only

image-etm-schwarzschild | verified | ETM Schwarzschild row
Source: image-etm, left row 1
Literal/normalized source: ds²=−(1−2M/r)dt²+(1−2M/r)^(−1)dr²+r²dΩ².
Domain: Schwarzschild exterior, G=c=1, M>0, r>2M; signature −+++.
Finding: Correct standalone exterior metric. Its adjoining ↔ Einstein–Rosen label does not establish a generic traversable Morris–Thorne geometry.
Adapter: standard-exterior-metric (horizon.metric 1 0 0 3 1.2)

image-etm-kerr-fragment | reference-only | ETM incomplete Kerr expression

Finding: The literal radial coefficient is Σ, missing /Δ; the dφ² term is absent. Do not execute this fragment or silently replace the printed terms.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Use the complete PDF Eq. (16) with Q=0, including g_rr=Σ/Δ and the dφ² coefficient.

image-etm-kn-fragment | reference-only | ETM malformed Kerr–Newman expression
Source: image-etm, left row 4
Literal/normalized source: ds²=−(1−2Mr−Q²/Σ)dt²−(4Mar sin²θ/Σ)dt dφ+Σdr²+Σdθ²+…
Domain: Printed fragment, not a well-formed KN line element.
Finding: As printed, g_tt lacks (2Mr−Q²)/Σ grouping; the mixed term omits its charge correction, g_rr lacks /Δ and dφ² is missing. The literal expression has inconsistent dimensions in its first parenthesis.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Complete KN: PDF Eq. (16). In expanded form, g_tt=−[1−(2Mr−Q²)/Σ], mixed ds² coefficient=−2a(2Mr−Q²)sin²θ/Σ, g_rr=Σ/Δ.
Adapter: reference-only
References: Adamo and Newman, The Kerr–Newman metric: A Review — https://arxiv.org/pdf/1410.6626

image-etm-er-label | refined | ETM generic throat ansatz labelled Einstein–Rosen

Domain: Static spherical Morris–Thorne-type ansatz, with functions Φ(r), b(r) not specified.
Finding: This is a generic throat ansatz, not the specific maximally extended Schwarzschild ER bridge. A traversable throat requires finite redshift/no horizon, flare-out and an appropriate stress-energy model; Schwarzschild ER is nontraversable.
Separate corrected/generalized expression: Retain as a generic static spherical throat ansatz; remove the asserted universal ER/Schwarzschild equivalence.
Adapter: reference-only

image-event-frame-dragging | refined | Event picture local frame angular velocity
Source: image-event-horizon, both bottom frame-dragging callouts

Domain: Stationary axisymmetric exterior; conventional coordinates and g_φφ≠0.
Finding: The conventional zero-angular-momentum observer formula is −g_tφ/g_φφ. This is local frame angular velocity, generally distinct from constant Ω_H and from a material body's spin. The uncertain image subscript is retained explicitly.

image-aperture-radius | toy-assumption | Phenomenological aperture radius
Source: image-aperture, aperture law
Literal/normalized source: r_A=r₀√[1−(a_c/a)²], a>a_c.
Domain: Real positive r₀ and threshold a_c; displayed branch a>a_c; same spin units for a and a_c.
Finding: This is a declared geometric response function, not an Einstein-equation solution. A zero radius for a≤a_c is an added piecewise simulation convention and must be documented. The printed formula alone is undefined at a=0.
Simulation convention: For a_c>0, set r_A=0 at/below threshold; use the printed branch only for a>a_c.
Adapter: toy-assumption (horizon.scenario {})

image-aperture-cover | toy-assumption | Cover threshold and integrated loading
Source: image-aperture, cover law
Literal/normalized source: C=Θ(σ_A−σ_seal); σ_A=∫_A ρ_aggie dA.
Domain: Declared scalar loading and sealing threshold; density meaning, measure and units require specification.
Finding: The integral is not executable without a density field/measure. σ_A is an integrated quantity: if ρ is surface mass density it is mass, not surface density; if volume density it has mass/length units. The scalar scenario may accept loading as input without claiming to solve this integral. Θ(0) is not specified in the image.
Simulation convention: The implementation defines Θ_seal(0)=1: equality seals. This is a selected convention, distinct from Θ_positive(0)=0 used for aperture/passage. Scalar loading is input, or a supplied finite surface-density patch sum is evaluated; no rho_aggie field is inferred.
Adapter: toy-assumption (horizon.scenario {})

Domain: Declared binary C and chosen Heaviside threshold convention; not a causal-geodesic result.
Finding: A Boolean rule for the proposed scenario. It does not demonstrate physical traversability, stability or absence of an event horizon.

Finding: Equivalent to the radius-based indicator only after the stated piecewise extension and Θ_positive(0)=0 convention. The source uses the same Θ glyph for the cover test, but the simulation separately declares Θ_seal(0)=1 for equality sealing. It is not an independently established master law of general relativity.

PRIMARY REFERENCE ACCESS AND LIMITS
Primary literature/author research used for qualifications. The original BCH link did not yield directly extractable web text; its first-law/Smarr statements were independently checked algebraically within KN and against Hawking's primary paper. For irreducible mass this registry uses the charged mass relation together with M_irr²=A/(16π) and direct algebra, rather than relying on imperfect web extraction of a solved expression.
